text: Energy-minimize a solvated alanine dipeptide (OPC water) before heating it: 2000 cycles in total, the first 1000 of them steepest descent, with an 8 Angstrom nonbonded cutoff.

quote: The last components needed are the input files that define the program settings for each MD run. For this system, we will perform an energy minimization on the system, then slowly heat the system, and then do production MD at the desired temperature and pressure. Sander will be used for minimization and heating and pmemd will be used for the actual production run.

text: Heat the minimized alanine dipeptide system from 0 K to 300 K at constant volume: 10,000 steps of 2 fs with SHAKE on bonds to hydrogen, starting fresh with no velocities. Use a Langevin thermostat with a 2 ps^-1 collision frequency and an 8 Angstrom cutoff, and ramp the thermostat's target temperature linearly from 0 K to 300 K over the first 9,000 steps, then hold it at 300 K for the last 1,000.
license: Copyright Ross Walker & Ben Madej, 2015 | All materials copyrighted by authors.
quote: The final three lines allow the thermostat to change its target temperature throughout the simulation. For the first 9000 steps, the temperature will increase from 0 K to 300 K. For steps 9001 to 10000, the temperature will remain at 300 K.

text: Run 10 ns of NPT production for the alanine dipeptide system (5,000,000 steps of 2 fs), continuing from the heating run's coordinates and velocities. SHAKE on bonds to hydrogen, Langevin thermostat at 300 K with a 2 ps^-1 collision frequency, isotropic pressure scaling with the Berendsen barostat, and an 8 Angstrom cutoff.
license: Copyright Ross Walker & Ben Madej, 2015 | All materials copyrighted by authors.
quote: The production time of this simulation will be 10 ns. Using a time step (dt) of 0.002 ps, a nstlim value of 5000000 will give us this simulation time.

text: Minimize the water and ions around the solvated RAMP1 extracellular domain while holding the protein (residues 1-81) in place with 100 kcal/mol/A^2 positional restraints: 1000 cycles, the first 20 steepest descent, in a constant-volume periodic box with a 10 Angstrom cutoff and SHAKE on bonds to hydrogen.
quote: The positions do not take into account the presence of the solute or ions. This input minimizes the energy of water and ions. Everything else in the system is restrained.

text: Heat the solvated RAMP1 system from 100 K to 298 K over 1 ns at constant volume (1,000,000 steps of 1 fs, SHAKE on bonds to hydrogen), starting fresh with velocities drawn at 100 K. Use a Langevin thermostat (collision frequency 1 ps^-1) whose target temperature ramps linearly from 100 K to 298 K across the whole run, an 8 Angstrom cutoff, and 100 kcal/mol/A^2 restraints on residues 1-81.
quote: This first step of relaxation will start the system from a low temperature of 100 K and gradually heat up to 298 K over 1 nanosecond of simulation time at a constant volume.

text: Continue the RAMP1 relaxation for 1 ns at constant pressure so the box density can relax (1,000,000 steps of 1 fs, SHAKE on bonds to hydrogen), restarting from the heating run's coordinates and velocities. Langevin thermostat at 298 K (collision frequency 1 ps^-1), Monte Carlo barostat with isotropic scaling, 8 Angstrom cutoff, and residues 1-81 still restrained at 100 kcal/mol/A^2.
quote: This second step of relaxation will maintain the system from at 298 K over 1 nanosecond of simulation time at a constant pressure, allowing the box density to relax.

text: Next RAMP1 relaxation step: 1 ns at constant pressure and 298 K (1,000,000 steps of 1 fs, SHAKE on bonds to hydrogen), restarting with the previous step's velocities, with the restraint on residues 1-81 lowered to 10 kcal/mol/A^2. Langevin thermostat with a 1 ps^-1 collision frequency, Monte Carlo barostat with isotropic scaling, 8 Angstrom cutoff.
quote: This third step of MD will run MD over 1 ns at constant pressure and 298 K with a smaller restraint of 10 kcal/mol•Å2.

text: Minimize the RAMP1 system again, now restraining only the protein backbone atoms (CA, N and C) at 10 kcal/mol/A^2: 1000 cycles with the first 30 steepest descent, constant-volume periodic box, 8 Angstrom cutoff, SHAKE on bonds to hydrogen.
quote: Minimization of the system with restraints only on the backbone of the protein. In earlier runs, all atoms of the protein were restrainted. Now it's just the backbone atoms.

text: After the backbone-restrained minimization, run 1 ns of constant-pressure MD at 298 K (1,000,000 steps of 1 fs, SHAKE on bonds to hydrogen), starting fresh with velocities assigned at 298 K. Restrain the backbone atoms CA, N and C at 10 kcal/mol/A^2, with a Langevin thermostat (collision frequency 1 ps^-1), the Monte Carlo barostat with isotropic scaling and an 8 Angstrom cutoff.
quote: Relaxation over 1 ns of simulation time at a constant pressure with backbone restraints set to 10 kcal/mol•Å2.

text: Continue the RAMP1 relaxation for 1 ns at constant pressure and 298 K from the previous step's coordinates and velocities, with the backbone (CA, N, C) restraints lowered to 1 kcal/mol/A^2. Use a 1 fs timestep with SHAKE on bonds to hydrogen, a Langevin thermostat (1 ps^-1), the Monte Carlo barostat with isotropic scaling and an 8 Angstrom cutoff.
quote: Relaxation for 1 ns of simulation time at a constant pressure with restraints on the backbone lowered to 1 kcal/mol•Å2.

text: Run another 1 ns of constant-pressure relaxation of RAMP1 at 298 K, restarting with velocities, and lower the backbone (CA, N, C) restraints to 0.1 kcal/mol/A^2. Use 1,000,000 steps of 1 fs with SHAKE on bonds to hydrogen, a Langevin thermostat with a 1 ps^-1 collision frequency, the Monte Carlo barostat with isotropic scaling and an 8 Angstrom cutoff.
quote: Relaxation for 1 ns of simulation time at a constant pressure with restraints on the backbone lowered to 0.1 kcal/mol•Å2.

text: Final RAMP1 relaxation step: remove all restraints and simulate 1 ns at constant pressure and 298 K (1,000,000 steps of 1 fs, SHAKE on bonds to hydrogen), restarting from the previous coordinates and velocities, with a Langevin thermostat (1 ps^-1), the Monte Carlo barostat with isotropic scaling and an 8 Angstrom cutoff.
quote: This last step of relaxation removes the restraints on the backbone,simulates 1 ns of simulation time at a constant pressure.

text: Run a 50 ns constant-pressure production simulation of the RAMP1 protein in a truncated octahedral box of explicit water, restarting from the equilibrated coordinates and velocities: 25,000,000 steps of 2 fs with SHAKE on bonds to hydrogen, a Langevin thermostat at 300 K with a 1 ps^-1 collision frequency, isotropic pressure scaling and a 9 Angstrom cutoff.
quote: These settings are appropriate for a short simulation (50 ns) of a protein system in a truncated octahedral box solvated in explicit water, but you may need to change some aspects of it for your own system.

text: Write the input for a 10 ns constant-pressure MD run of the solvated RAMP1 protein (truncated octahedral box), continuing from a restart with velocities: 2 fs steps with SHAKE on bonds to hydrogen, a 300 K Langevin thermostat (collision frequency 1 ps^-1), isotropic pressure scaling and a 9 Angstrom cutoff.

text: Minimize a B-DNA polyA-polyT decamer in vacuum (no periodic box, no implicit solvent) before MD: 500 cycles, the first 250 steepest descent, with a 12 Angstrom nonbonded cutoff.
quote: To create our input file: To turn on minimization, we specify IMIN = 1. We want a fairly short minimization since we don't actually need to reach the minima, but just want to move away from any local maxima, so we select 500 steps of minimization by specifying MAXCYC = 500.

text: Run 100 ps of MD on the DNA decamer in vacuum (no periodic box, no implicit solvent) with a 12 Angstrom cutoff: 100,000 steps of 1 fs, a Langevin thermostat at 300 K with a 1 ps^-1 collision frequency, and initial velocities assigned at 300 K.
quote: The CUT variable specifies the cut off range for the long range non-bonded interactions. Here, two different values for the cutoff will be used, one run with a cut off of 12 angstroms (CUT = 12.0) and one run without a cutoff. To run without a cutoff we simply set CUT to be larger than the extent of the system (e.g. CUT = 999).

text: Minimize the whole solvated DNA decamer system (TIP3P water, Na+ counterions) with no restraints: 2500 cycles, the first 1000 steepest descent, in a constant-volume periodic box with a 10 Angstrom cutoff.
quote: Now we have minimized the water and ions the next stage of our minimization is to minimize the entire system. In this case we will run 2,500 steps of minimization without the restraints this time.
note: The Rizzo 2008 oxytocin tutorial's whole-system minimization is the same file and was dropped.

text: The solvated DNA decamer has been heated at constant volume; now switch to constant pressure (1 bar, isotropic scaling, 2 ps pressure relaxation time) and run 100 ps of unrestrained MD (50,000 steps of 2 fs with SHAKE on bonds to hydrogen), continuing from the previous coordinates and velocities. Use a Langevin thermostat at 300 K with a 1 ps^-1 collision frequency and a 10 Angstrom cutoff.
quote: Now that we have successfully heated our system at constant volume with weak restraints on the DNA, the next stage is to switch to using constant pressure so that the density of our water can relax. At the same time we can safely remove the restraints on our DNA, because we are at 300 K . We will run this equilibration for 100 ps to give our system plenty of time to relax.

text: Write one 200 ps segment of constant-pressure MD for a solvated A-DNA polyA-polyT decamer (TIP3P, Na+), to be repeated nine times for 1.8 ns in total. It restarts from the previous segment's coordinates and velocities and runs 100,000 steps of 2 fs with SHAKE on bonds to hydrogen. Use 1 bar with isotropic scaling and a 2 ps pressure relaxation time, a Langevin thermostat at 300 K (1 ps^-1), a 10 Angstrom cutoff and no restraints.
quote: In the next stage of our simulation we are going to run a further 1.8 ns of MD. Rather than run a separate equilibration and production phase we will, for convenience, combine the two since our production conditions will be identical to our final equilibration conditions.

text: Equilibrate the solvated PPAT-pantetheine protein system for 100 ns at constant pressure and temperature to adjust the density: 50,000,000 steps of 2 fs with SHAKE on bonds to hydrogen, restarting from the heating run's coordinates and velocities, 1 bar with isotropic scaling and a 2 ps pressure relaxation time, a Langevin thermostat at 300 K (collision frequency 1 ps^-1), a 10 Angstrom cutoff and no restraints.
quote: Then the systems are equilibrated for 100 ns under constant pressure and temperature (NPT) to adjust the system density; followed by 100 ns production simulations under constant volume and temperature (NVT) conditions.
note: Source gained a final newline: the page ends the block with '/' and pmemd 26 stops with 'End of file' without one.

text: Run 100 ns of production MD for the PPAT-pantetheine system at constant volume and temperature (NVT), continuing from the NPT equilibration's coordinates and velocities: 50,000,000 steps of 2 fs with SHAKE on bonds to hydrogen, a Langevin thermostat at 300 K with a 1 ps^-1 collision frequency, a 10 Angstrom cutoff and no restraints.
quote: Then the systems are equilibrated for 100 ns under constant pressure and temperature (NPT) to adjust the system density; followed by 100 ns production simulations under constant volume and temperature (NVT) conditions.
note: Source gained a final newline: the page ends the block with '/' and pmemd 26 stops with 'End of file' without one.

text: Relax a solvated protein (PDB 1RGG, chain A) by energy minimization: 1000 cycles of conjugate gradient, with the backbone atoms CA, N and O of residues 1-96 held by 10 kcal/mol/A^2 positional restraints.
tutorial: Running Molecular Dynamics Simulations with AMBER
quote: Before simulating a system we need to relax it. Any atomic clashes must be resolved, and potential energy minimized to avoid unphysically large forces that can crash a simulation.

text: Heat the minimized 1RGG protein system from 150 K to 300 K: 10,000 MD steps, starting fresh with velocities assigned at 150 K, using the Berendsen thermostat with its target held at 300 K throughout (no ramp) and a 1 ps coupling time constant, no barostat (constant volume), and 10 kcal/mol/A^2 restraints on the backbone atoms CA, N and O of residues 1-96.
tutorial: Running Molecular Dynamics Simulations with AMBER
quote: In the examples bonds with hydrogens are not constrained and the default timestep of 1 fs in used. To turn on SHAKE use ntf=2 and ntc=2.
note: The file sets no timestep or SHAKE (pmemd's defaults: 1 fs, no constraints), so the prompt leaves both to the model.

text: Equilibrate the heated 1RGG system at constant pressure for 5,000 steps, restarting from the heating run's coordinates and velocities: Berendsen thermostat at 300 K (1 ps time constant), Berendsen barostat at 1 bar with isotropic scaling and a 1 ps relaxation time, and the backbone CA, N and O atoms of residues 1-96 restrained at 10 kcal/mol/A^2.
tutorial: Running Molecular Dynamics Simulations with AMBER
quote: Turn on restart flag.
note: The file sets no timestep or SHAKE, so the prompt leaves both to the model.

text: Continue equilibrating the 1RGG system without restraints for 1,000,000 steps, restarting with velocities, using a Langevin thermostat at 300 K (collision frequency 1 ps^-1) and the Berendsen barostat at 1 bar (isotropic scaling, 1 ps relaxation time).
tutorial: Running Molecular Dynamics Simulations with AMBER
quote: Use Langevin thermostat + Berendsen barostat. Simulate on GPU
note: The file sets no timestep or SHAKE, so the prompt leaves both to the model.

text: Run the oxytocin production dynamics in explicit water at 300 K and 1 bar: 250 ps (125,000 steps of 2 fs with SHAKE on bonds to hydrogen), continuing from the equilibration's coordinates and velocities, with a Langevin thermostat (collision frequency 1 ps^-1), isotropic pressure scaling with a 2 ps relaxation time, a 10 Angstrom cutoff and no restraints.
quote: Step 4. Production Run - Run the production dynamics at 300 K and 1 bar pressure.

text: Minimize the solvated HIV protease-inhibitor complex (PDB 1HVR) for 1000 cycles of steepest descent, holding the heavy atoms of residues 1-199 with 5 kcal/mol/A^2 restraints, in a constant-volume periodic box with an 8 Angstrom cutoff and no bond constraints.
quote: Before running any equilibration and production, we have to minimize the energy of system. This process can remove any unfavorable interaction between atoms due to the low resolution of biomolecule. If an unfavorable interaction is present when doing equilibration and production, atoms may "fly apart" and "crash" into other part of the biomolecule.

text: Run the unrestrained production simulation of the solvated 4QMZ protein-ligand complex: 2 ns (1,000,000 steps of 2 fs with SHAKE on bonds to hydrogen), restarting from equilibration with velocities, at constant pressure with the Berendsen barostat (isotropic scaling, 0.5 ps relaxation time) and a Langevin thermostat at 298.15 K (collision frequency 2 ps^-1), 8 Angstrom cutoff.
quote: Change your directory to 003.production. Once here, create two new directories, 001.restrained and 002.unrestrained. The simulation will be run twice, once with a restraint on the backbone and once with no restraint.

text: First preparation step for the solvated 3WZE complex: minimize only the hydrogens by restraining every non-hydrogen atom at 5 kcal/mol/A^2. Run 5000 cycles of steepest descent in a constant-volume periodic box with an 8 Angstrom cutoff and no bond constraints.
quote: Next, we will minimize and equilibrate the system over nine successive steps. For information about the different parameters see the AMBER16 manual.

text: Equilibration step 7 for the solvated 1NDV complex: 50 ps of constant-pressure MD (50,000 steps of 1 fs, no bond constraints), restarting with velocities from step 6. Restrain the heavy atoms of residues 1-350 at 0.5 kcal/mol/A^2, and use the Berendsen barostat (isotropic scaling, 0.5 ps relaxation time), a Langevin thermostat at 298.15 K (collision frequency 2 ps^-1) and an 8 Angstrom cutoff.
quote: Before we run a production simulation, we must first minimize and equilibrate the system. We will do this with a 9-step procedure. This process will minimize the energy of the structure, slowly heat the system to the desired temperature, and then equilibrate the system at that temperature.

text: Minimize the solvated 1G2L protein-ligand complex with the heavy atoms of residues 1-292 restrained at 5 kcal/mol/A^2, so mainly hydrogens, water and ions relax: 5000 cycles, the first 2500 steepest descent, in a constant-volume periodic box with an 8 Angstrom cutoff and no bond constraints.
quote: This step removes steric clashes and relaxes high-energy contacts, particularly involving hydrogen atoms, while keeping the heavy atoms restrained.

text: Run a short MD stage that heats and equilibrates the minimized 1G2L complex at constant pressure: 50 ps (50,000 steps of 1 fs, no bond constraints) starting from the minimized coordinates without velocities, a Langevin thermostat targeting 298.15 K (collision frequency 2 ps^-1), the Berendsen barostat (isotropic scaling, 0.5 ps relaxation time), an 8 Angstrom cutoff, and the heavy atoms of residues 1-292 restrained at 5 kcal/mol/A^2.
quote: In this step, we run a short MD simulation to heat and equilibrate the system under constant pressure while restraining all heavy atoms.
note: The tutorial says all heavy atoms are restrained; the mask restrains those of residues 1-292 only, and the prompt follows the file.

text: Equilibrate the 1G2L complex at constant pressure (1 bar, isotropic scaling, 0.5 ps relaxation time) with weak 1 kcal/mol/A^2 restraints on the heavy atoms of residues 1-292: 100 ps as 50,000 steps of 2 fs with SHAKE on bonds to hydrogen, starting fresh from coordinates only, with a Langevin thermostat at 298.15 K (collision frequency 2 ps^-1) and an 8 Angstrom cutoff.
quote: In this step, we run MD under constant pressure with weak restraints on heavy atoms. This allows the system to equilibrate more naturally while maintaining the overall structural integrity.
note: The file starts this equilibration step fresh (irest=0, ntx=1); the prompt follows the file.

text: Equilibrate the 1G2L complex for 50 ps at constant pressure, restarting with velocities, restraining only the protein backbone atoms CA, C and N of residues 1-291 at 0.1 kcal/mol/A^2 so the ligand moves freely. Use 50,000 steps of 1 fs with no bond constraints, the Berendsen barostat (isotropic scaling, 0.5 ps relaxation time), a Langevin thermostat at 298.15 K (2 ps^-1) and an 8 Angstrom cutoff.
quote: In this step, we restrain only the protein backbone atoms (CA, C, N). Since the ligand is typically the last residue, we restrain residues 1–291 (protein only) while allowing the ligand to move freely.

text: Run 10 ns of production MD for the 1G2L complex (5,000,000 steps of 2 fs with SHAKE on bonds to hydrogen), restarting from the last equilibration's coordinates and velocities, with weak 0.1 kcal/mol/A^2 restraints on the backbone atoms CA, C and N of residues 1-291. Constant pressure with the Berendsen barostat (isotropic scaling, 0.5 ps relaxation time), a Langevin thermostat at 298.15 K (collision frequency 2 ps^-1), 8 Angstrom cutoff.
quote: After completing equilibration, the final restart file 09md.rst7 is used as the starting structure for the production MD simulation. This step runs a longer MD simulation while applying weak restraints to the protein backbone.

text: Minimize the solvent around the solvated MTR1 ribozyme: 500 cycles of conjugate gradient with a 12 Angstrom cutoff, restraining the solute heavy atoms (every non-hydrogen atom except the NA, CL and MG ions and WAT water) at 50 kcal/mol/A^2.
